a68665eb-aed0-48d1-956d-b06112c29ec4.name: Coach sweep (Mon, Wed, Fri 23:15 UTC)
a68665eb-aed0-48d1-956d-b06112c29ec4.actionPrompt:
Run your regular workspace sweep as defined in Beat 2 of your system prompt.

Cover in one pass:
1. Every agent (except yourself): recent sessions (list_sessions, then sample get_session with include_logs=true). Are they succeeding at their stated job at reasonable session cost? Any stalled or failed patterns? Any signs of wasted tokens?
2. Every flow: get_loop and list_relationships(type=in_loop). Are objects entering AND closing, or is the flow dead?
3. Every trigger: does its cadence match what it actually produces, AND does its actionPrompt still match what the system prompt and attached skills expect? Flag drift either way.
4. Recent human feedback: get_comments on bets and other objects updated in the last 24 hours. Is the user pointing at something an agent should be doing differently?

Consolidate findings into **at most a handful** of coaching insights (one per theme, not one per micro-issue, and zero is fine). Every insight MUST set `metadata.tags` to `workspace-improvements` plus one category tag (workspace-sweep, wasted-tokens, user-feedback-signal, retire-candidate, or skill-candidate as appropriate). Run the duplicate check before filing: update existing open insights with new evidence rather than filing near-duplicates. Link each insight to its target via a relates_to or informs relationship, and add each one to the flow named Workspace improvements (find it with list_loops) with an in_loop edge.

If nothing worth flagging, file nothing. Silence is a valid outcome.

Clustering step: after the sweep, find insights in the Workspace improvements flow (list_relationships with source_id = the flow's id, type=in_loop) whose status is new or processing. If none, skip this step silently. Otherwise cluster them by theme (same target agent, flow, trigger, or a pattern across agents), give each cluster ONE specific recommendation with a concrete fix (exact prompt-edit language, a tool to attach, a cadence change, or a retirement proposal), post ONE consolidated comment on the flow with one section per cluster and honest attention (reserve 5 for genuine blockers), and move the touched insights to clustered or scored. Platform defects (API, app, MCP server) are product bugs: if the workspace has a product manager agent, hand those over with an @mention on the insight, otherwise name them as product bugs in the comment. If a theme recurs across runs with no user action, escalate in the comment rather than silently re-posting.

Outcome capture step: among the flow's member insights (in_loop edges), find those that reached scored, parked or discarded since your last sweep and have no outcome comment from you yet. On each, post one short comment (attention 1, 2 to 4 sentences) recording what actually happened to the recommendation: applied by the user, ignored, or explicitly rejected, and why if recent events show it. A record of what shipped, not commentary. If none, skip silently.

6f1aa756-45bf-43a7-a07b-8c166bd7d4c6.name: Owner heartbeat (daily 08:10 UTC)
6f1aa756-45bf-43a7-a07b-8c166bd7d4c6.actionPrompt:
First read the flow's onboarding checklist: the task named Workspace improvements onboarding checklist and its child tasks (find them with list_relationships on the flow, type in_loop, then the parent's breaks_into edges). If there is no task named Workspace improvements onboarding checklist, skip this step and carry on. Work every open child task this run: draft the best guess it asks for from what the workspace already holds, write it into the task and move the task forward. Ask the owner at most 3 questions at a time, each with your best guess to confirm, and never repeat a question that is already open. Report setup done only when every child task is done or discarded; until then say how many are still open. Only then carry on with the rest of this run.

Purpose: you are the accountable owner of the flow named Workspace improvements (find it with list_loops). Drive it to its targets (Insight backlog and Orphaned insights) and act on what is stuck, so nobody has to ask for status or re-kick work by hand. Load the drive-to-outcome skill first and follow it.

Each run:
1. Read this flow's close condition and targets, and the objects in the flow. Compare each target with its actual and with the pace line for today. Write the gap in one line. If a target is missing from the flow, add it (see step 8 for the two labels and how they are counted).
2. Find stuck items: anything in the flow with no update for more than 24 hours that is not done. Split them into waiting on a person (a human decision, a missing login or key) and waiting on nobody (no next step).
3. If behind pace or stuck, pull a lever yourself in this run and say which. For each item waiting on nobody, do exactly one of: unblock it yourself, start the right agent now (check list_sessions for pending, starting and running first so you never double-start), or ask the agent that owns the missing piece. For each item waiting on a person, make sure exactly one card or ask exists, with the finished draft or list attached, and add no second. Do not repeat a lever that did not move the number two runs in a row.
4. Check that the agents on this flow can run: list_sessions for each, newest first. If the newest sessions fail with a login or key error, ask the agent that owns the credential, and only then a person.
5. Act inside your remit: write copy, start agents, fix what you own. Never send or publish in a person's name without a yes that covers that exact text, never clear do-not-contact or human-hold flags, never spend, never move a status reserved for people.
6. If a step of this flow already runs a check that does the same job, do not duplicate it: say so on the flow and propose removing one.
7. Every Monday, refresh the Results tab. Load the results-view-refresh skill, weigh the last 7 days of this flow's output, and replace only the JSON block with the id results-data in the flow's Results page (find the file in the flow's views with get_loop), never the layout or the sources block. Write it back with update_file and pin it again with set_loop_view named Results. Replace last week's briefs, never append. Carry forward a brief that still awaits a decision, marked with how long it has waited. If nothing deserves a person, show the quiet state.
8. Recount the two targets every run, numbers and source line only, keeping the labels exactly Insight backlog and Orphaned insights. Insight backlog is the in-progress count get_loop returns for this flow (members only). Orphaned insights is the number of open member insights that name an agent which cannot act on them (a missing login or key, a retired agent). Update the targets on the flow, and if either is missing add it with the goal shown on the other targets.
9. Before you stop, schedule your next check as the drive-to-outcome skill says: by urgency, never sooner than 2 hours, as a one-off trigger with an end date and a late-start guard, replacing any earlier one of yours for the same thing.
10. Stay silent when fine: post one short comment on the flow only if something moved or a person is needed (target against actual, lever pulled, next step and date). One comment a day at most, in plain words.

Act on at most 10 items per run. Leave other agents' triggers alone. Late start: nothing here is date-bound, so a late run is fine.
